header: # antt-msliv0638-brochado-1712 appendix (m0280-296), decoded against key.tsv (a period key rebuilt by
# us from the appendix's own contemporary Deciffrada glosses -- key source grade 'period', PX-BROKEY
# + PX-BROKEY2, 25 Sept 2026). This is the control described in NOTES.md 'PX-BROKEY2': the key must
# re-read its own source. It is NOT a rule-7 reading of anything beyond the appendix itself -- there is
# no spec/judge for this target yet, and every entry here is already given in plaintext by the
# manuscript's own Deciffrada line (see plaintext_appendix.tsv); see conflicts.tsv for the per-entry
# agreement between this decode and that plaintext.
# tokens {total}: {HCSMIU} (U = code with no key.tsv row; M = key value held by <65% majority)
# antt-msliv0638-brochado-1712 body cipher runs (outside the appendix m0279-296), decoded against the
# same key.tsv the appendix's own Deciffrada glosses built (key source grade 'period', PX-BROKEY/
# PX-BROKEY2/PX-BROGLYPH). m0179-r1/m0180-r1 (letters 80/81) are CONTROLS: the appendix already carries
# their plaintext (Carta 80/81) independently of this key, so their agreement with plaintext_appendix.tsv
# is a check on the key, not a reading. m0275-r1+m0276-r1+m0276-r2 (letter 134) has no appendix entry
# (past Carta 123, the appendix's highest) -- this is the genuine candidate reading (PX-BRODEC, 25 Sept
# 2026). Grade combines the key's own per-code grade (key.tsv 'grade' column) with this file's own
# transcription-pass grade (its 'conf' column, added by scripts/09_body_prep.py from the existing
# 'grade' column): a token grades C only when both the code is grade C in key.tsv AND the transcription
# agreed (conf=H); either one at M pulls the token down to M; an unkeyed code (no key.tsv row, mostly the
# unresolved ff?/dd?/+? glyphs) grades U, shown as the unkeyed marker below.
